messages:
olivia: Hi team, after upgrading to @redwood/sdk v0.23.0 our Node app started returning 404 for the chat route that used to work. No code changes other than the dependency. Happening in prod and staging.

olivia: Example error: 
```
HTTP 404 GET /v1/chat.generate
{ error: 'route not found' }
```

olivia: Also seeing occasional 401 on retries (we're using retry middleware) — looks like a token header gets dropped on retry?

jamie: Sorry about that — can you paste the SDK version from package.json and the exact API call you make?

olivia: package.json: 
```
"dependencies": { "@redwood/sdk": "0.23.0" }
```
Request code (simplified):
```
const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY });
await client.chat.create({ model: 'redwood/fast-chat', messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'hi' }] });
```

olivia: Same code using v0.22.1 works fine.

lin: Ok — two things to check quickly: 1) v0.23 changed some route names (we renamed chat.create -> chat.generate in the runtime but kept a shim in some releases), 2) retry lib we use strips auth on 307/302 redirects in some Node versions. Can you run with DEBUG env to capture request/response headers?

olivia: Pasted sensitive-stripped logs: 
```
-> POST /v1/chat.generate
Authorization: Bearer REDACTED
Content-Type: application/json
{ model: 'redwood/fast-chat', messages: [...] }
<- 404 { error: 'route not found' }
-> POST /v1/chat.generate (retry)
Authorization: (missing)
<- 401 { error: 'unauthorized' }
```

olivia: So second request lost Authorization header. We saw this happen only after upgrade.

jamie: Thanks — that aligns with an SDK bug where the client constructor route mapping was accidentally dropped when packaging the ESM build. We'll escalate. Can you confirm whether you're using CommonJS (require) or ESM (import)?

olivia: We bundle with webpack into CJS for Lambda (require).

lin: Got it. Can you try temporary workaround: pin to 0.22.1 and set an env var to force route aliasing? E.g. RW_LEGACY_ROUTE_SHIM=1 — this should restore the old chat.create mapping and avoid the 404. Also disable retry for now or use a retry that preserves headers.

olivia: Quick repro steps I used for the team:
1) npm i @redwood/sdk@0.23.0
2) deploy to staging (CJS bundle)
3) call client.chat.create
4) observe 404 and then 401 on retry

olivia: Workaround test: downgraded to 0.22.1 -> all good.

jamie: We'll cut a patch. For tracking: assigning to eng-runtime, priority P1. Lin, can you take initial triage? I'll open a ticket.

lin: On it. Initial plan: reproduce in a minimal CJS Lambda, inspect published package exports, and add a test to the packager to ensure shims survive bundling.

deploy-bot: New issue created: RW-ISSUE-4381 "v0.23.0 CJS build missing route shim causing 404 + header loss on retry" (assignee: lin) :rocket:

jamie: Olivia — ETA for patch? We'll try to ship a 0.23.1 within 24 hours or provide a scoped patch you can apply. In the meantime please pin to 0.22.1 and remove automatic retry. Sorry for the disruption. :pray:

olivia: Thanks. Appreciate the quick response. Will confirm after we pin and disable retry.

lin: Note for repro: sample minimal client to reproduce locally:
```
const { RedwoodClient } = require('@redwood/sdk');
const c = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: 'x' });
c.chat.create({ model: 'redwood/fast-chat', messages:[{role:'user',content:'hi'}] });
```
Add node v18 and simulate Lambda-like bundling.

jamie: Follow-up: if anyone else hits this, please post here with runtime, bundler, and whether you saw 401 only on retry. We'll collect and link to RW-ISSUE-4381.
